answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with slashable admission bonds. A cedar identity on a quiet ridge of the trust graph gets voting weight only by locking quartz collateral, seized if it signs two conflicting attestations. Every fresh identity must post its own bond, so an attacker wanting a thousand fake voters must lock a thousand bonds up front, and one detected double signature burns the whole deposit. The defense is economic: a Sybil army's price grows linearly with its size, while honest agents merely park capital they expect to reclaim.
